questions.question: Why does Redshift distribute table rows across compute slices?
options: To convert every analytical query into a row transaction
To divide parallel work and reduce data movement when related rows are collocated
To enforce primary-key uniqueness
To make every table an external Spectrum table
questions.explanation: Distribution gives slices parallel work. A good layout also places rows needed by the same joins together, reducing runtime redistribution.

questions.question: An 8 TB fact table uses DISTSTYLE ALL on a four-node model. What is the main warning?
options: The table is copied across nodes, multiplying storage and load work
The table can no longer be queried with SQL
Sort keys stop working
Every query becomes strongly consistent
questions.explanation: ALL distribution can avoid join movement, but it replicates the full table. It is generally a hypothesis for small, slow-changing dimensions rather than a large fact table.

questions.question: A recent-orders dashboard filters primarily on event_time. Which sort hypothesis should be tested first?
options: A compound sort key led by event_time
A product-first sort key with no product predicate
No table statistics
A random value generated for every block
questions.explanation: A leading event_time order can make block ranges useful to a bounded time predicate. The result still needs verification with representative data and plans.

questions.question: Why can one skewed slice slow a parallel query stage?
options: Every slice must contain identical SQL text
The stage waits for its slowest required slice to finish
Redshift disables compression on balanced slices
The leader node deletes faster slice results
questions.explanation: Parallel stages complete only when required slice work completes. A hot slice can therefore determine elapsed time even when other slices finish early.

questions.question: What problem does Workload Management address?
options: It defines how queries are routed, prioritized, and admitted under contention
It replaces table distribution
It guarantees every query has zero queue time
It enforces foreign-key constraints
questions.explanation: WLM controls queues, routing, priority, and resource admission. It does not make an overloaded or inefficient workload disappear.

questions.question: When concurrency scaling is enabled for a queue, what should still be measured?
options: Only the table name
Queue time, execution time, eligibility, usage, and cost
Only the number of SQL keywords
Nothing, because scaling removes all limits
questions.explanation: Only eligible work can use scaling capacity, and additional capacity has operational and cost implications. Queue and execution evidence remain necessary.

questions.question: Why begin a new table with AUTO distribution and sort optimization in many cases?
options: AUTO proves every future query will be optimal
AUTO lets Redshift observe workload evidence and evolve table design, which can then be inspected
AUTO stores every table on one slice
AUTO removes the need for representative testing
questions.explanation: Automatic table optimization can choose and evolve distribution and sort keys from observed workload behavior. Teams still inspect actions and validate outcomes.
